title: Swan Lake (Scene theme)
description: The haunting oboe theme that opens Act II of Tchaikovsky's ballet, in B minor. A singing long-note melody that rises from the opening F-sharp and sways in dotted rhythms; it teaches legato phrasing and a steady accompaniment under a sustained line.

arrangements.label: Beginner
arrangements.notes: The eight-bar Swan theme written out twice, single-note melody with its dotted-quarter/eighth sway, over a left hand of open-fifth dyads (B-F#, with E-B touches) in half notes.
teachingPoints: Right hand sits with the thumb on B4 and the 5th finger on F#5 (1-2-3-4-5 = B C# D E F#); bar 1 holds F#5 for two beats, then the four eighths B-C#-D-E climb back up to it.
Bars 2-3 are the dotted sway: dotted-quarter F#5 then an eighth; in bar 3 the thumb drops to G4 for one note (fingers 5-2-4-2-1-4) and returns.
Bar 4: hold B4 through the tie into beat 3, then E-D-C# eighths lead back to the F#5 of bar 5; bar 8 is a whole-note B4 before the repeat.
Left hand plays only two open fifths, B2-F#3 and E3-B3 (5-1); the E-B dyad arrives on beat 3 of bars 1 and 4 only.

arrangements.label: Intermediate
arrangements.notes: The Swan theme followed by its real second strain, over a flowing eighth-note broken-chord left hand (root-fifth-octave-third), with the long notes thickened into thirds in bars 5-7 and 10-11.
teachingPoints: Left hand: one four-note arpeggio per half bar (5-3-2-1); learn the shapes Bm (B-F#-B-D), Em (E-B-E-G), D (D-A-D-F#) and F#7 (F#-C#-F#-A#) separately, then the changes in bars 10-12.
Right hand bars 5-7: hold the D5 under the long F#5 (fingers 3 and 5) while the eighths move; keep the dyad quieter than the melody note.
Bars 9-11 climb into a new position (C#5 D5 E5 = 1-2-3, then A5 and B5 with 5); bar 12 drops back to the opening position (F#5 D5 C#5 B4 = 5-3-2-1) after B5 with 4.
Keep the melody above the accompaniment: left hand pp and even, right hand singing; the A-sharp in the bar-12 and bar-16 left hand is the dominant leading back to B minor.
